transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-09-17
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Priya Khandelwal (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhao (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO, Helion), Ava Rodriguez (Partnerships, Helion), Miles Turner (Infra Lead, Helion)

Summary: quick partner intro, explore integration pattern for Helion's edge connector to offer Redwood inference as a channel/reseller option; discuss pilot scope, security/compliance requirements, latency/cost targets, and next steps. Helion is focused on regulated telco customers and wants private/VPC onramp for low-latency at the edge.

Topics: Partner model (reseller vs co-host), onramp connector architecture, security (SOC2, SSO), pilot success criteria, capacity and routing, billing/rev share, marketplace listing.

Action items (captured above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Priya Khandelwal: hey thanks everyone for joining, um we're excited to explore how Redwood can plug into Helion's edge connector offering, i think this is priya from redwood, im joined by ethan, our se.
[00:10] Samir Patel: hi priya, thanks. yeah this is samir, and ava, miles are on, appreciate the time. quick context — Helion runs a lightweight edge hypervisor that routes inference to local gpu clusters in telco POPs, we want to evaluate partner options to surface LLM inference to our customers without rebuilding inference stack.
[00:28] Ethan Zhao: great, so probably useful if i sketch the two integration patterns we usually see. one is a simple api-onramp: helion proxies requests to Redwood hosted api with tokenized tenant mapping. the other is a private deployment option — Redwood Private — where we ship a control plane and you run a dedicated inference footprint in your VPC or on prem.
[00:45] Miles Turner: couple quick constraints from infra side — some of our sites have spotty upstream, so we need good offline caching or small model fallbacks; also we have strict data residency for telco customers in EU and APAC.
[01:05] Priya Khandelwal: totally understood. for the host vs private tradeoff: hosted gives fastest time to market but you lose some network locality; private gives you VPC/onprem and KMS integration but adds ops. we can also support a hybrid where critical tenants are pinned to a private pool and others hit hosted.
[01:28] Ava Rodriguez: commercial question up front — is there partner pricing for a reseller/channel model? we want to list a co-branded offering in our marketplace.
[01:38] Priya Khandelwal: yes, we have channel terms; i'll send the one-pager. typical pilots are usage-based with an option for reserved capacity if throughput is predictable.
[01:46] Samir Patel: ok, on security — we need SOC2, iso27001, SAML/SSO support, audit logs, and preferably HSM/KMS where keys are customer-managed. can you confirm?
[01:58] Ethan Zhao: we are SOC2 Type II, we have ISO in progress, we support SAML SSO, RBAC, and we integrate with customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest; small note: our current HSM integrations are via partner KMS gateways — we can detail that in the security pack.
[02:15] Priya Khandelwal: disclaimer — some of that integration depends on the deployment mode. our hosted api supports customer-managed keys via a gateway, but pure onprem with local HSM will require additional work and an enterprise contract.
[02:29] Miles Turner: understood. for latency we typically target p50 < 200ms for text gen on small prompt sizes at edge sites — can redwood meet that with a hosted route?
[02:40] Ethan Zhao: for hosted from a remote region it's hard to guarantee 200ms if the client is at a telco POP; that's where private or dedicated pools come in. we can do aggressive batching and kv caching to reduce token costs but network RTT is the limiting factor. with a dedicated small cluster in-region we can often hit sub-150ms p50 for quantized models.
[03:02] Samir Patel: when you say quantized models — will there be a hit on output quality? some of our customers care about hallucination rates.
[03:09] Ethan Zhao: good question — quantization can slightly affect calibration, but modern 4-bit and int8 flows preserve most quality for retrieval augmented generation and many prompt patterns. part of the pilot will include quality evals on your prompt set so we can measure regressions.
[03:25] Ava Rodriguez: ok pilot — what does success look like to you from redwood's perspective? and what do we need to commit from helion?
[03:34] Priya Khandelwal: for a partner pilot we usually look for: 1) functional integration (end-to-end request flow through the onramp), 2) latency and cost benchmarks on a representative workload, 3) security sign-offs (SOC2 + basic SAML test), and 4) a marketing dev: marketplace listing or joint case study commitment if successful. on your side we'd need a staging cluster + sample traffic and an internal sponsor (ct0/infra) — seems like miles is that.
[04:00] Miles Turner: yep i can own infra and share a staging cluster. timeline wise we want an internal demo within 3 weeks and customer trials in 2 months.
[04:12] Priya Khandelwal: sounds reasonable. quick technical Q from ethan: how do you currently route ML workloads at the edge — are you containerizing models or mounting a model store?
[04:20] Miles Turner: we use a small container runtime and a model cache on local NVMe; models are fetched from our model registry when cold and we keep hot models pinned. we also have limited GPU multiplexing — mostly 4x A100-ish equivalents but some sites are pre-T4.
[04:36] Ethan Zhao: that maps well to our dedicated footprint. our runtime can either be deployed as a lightweight adapter that calls the redwood control plane or run fully on your infra in private mode. one note: our KV cache behavior expects steady prefix reuse; if your traffic is very spiky we might recommend auto-scaling or smaller buckets to avoid cold starts.
[04:56] Samir Patel: pricing detail — for telco customers usage can be huge during events; do you throttle or have burst policies?
[05:03] Priya Khandelwal: we support reserved capacity contracts plus burst capacity for sudden spikes; for channel partners we can model rev share on reserved blocks or offer dynamic passthrough billing. i'll put examples in the pricing doc.
[05:16] Ava Rodriguez: compliance question — will audit logs include per-token traces or just request-level metadata? our compliance team usually asks for request traces for 90 days.
[05:27] Ethan Zhao: by default we store request metadata and partial token metrics, full per-token transcripts are configurable and can be forwarded to your own logging endpoint. retention windows can be negotiated under enterprise terms.
[05:40] PR/Market question from Ava: we want a simple integration flow for our partners — can you provide an SDK or helm chart for the connector?
[05:49] Ethan Zhao: yes we have an official helm chart and a light-weight sdk for Golang and Python; we can share a reference connector that maps your tenant auth to Redwood API keys. some of the helm values will differ by deployment mode, we'll document that.
[06:05] Samir Patel: technical deep dive — can you run a quick sketch of the network hop diagram and where keys live in each pattern?
[06:12] Ethan Zhao: sure. (flips to shared slide link) pattern A: Helion edge -> Helion control plane -> Redwood Hosted API (token mapping) -> Redwood runtime in hosted region. keys: stored in Redwood KMS gateway for customer keys; minimal footprint on Helion. Pattern B: Helion edge -> Helion network -> Redwood private control plane in your VPC -> local runtime. keys: customer-managed KMS, HSM behind your VPC. I'll drop these diagrams in the follow up.
[06:40] Miles Turner: any known gotchas for edge deployment? i'm thinking about GPU driver mismatch, kernel versions, and pinned model weights filling nvme.
[06:49] Ethan Zhao: yes drivers are the usual pain point, we provide a validated set of container images and an onboarding matrix. nvme pressure is solved with model eviction policies and we can recommend a quantization profile to reduce cache footprint.
[07:02] Samir Patel: what about offline inference when the edge loses connectivity to the control plane? we'd like a degraded but functional mode.
[07:11] Priya Khandelwal: we support a disconnected mode where a local runtime can perform inference for a bounded set of models and fall back to a smaller model family if it cannot reach control plane. it's part of the private/offline roadmap — we'll need to scope that for the pilot.
[07:26] Ava Rodriguez: go-to-market — if the pilot goes well, how quickly can we have a marketplace listing?
[07:33] Priya Khandelwal: once the integration passes security and basic functional checks, marketplace listing can be turned on in 2-3 weeks. we have standard partner co-branding materials.
[07:42] Samir Patel: competitor question — we've seen offerings from ApexFusion that do onramp and OronWave that promises on-prem orchestration. where does redwood differentiate for a partner like us?
[07:54] Ethan Zhao: our focus is production economics and predictable serving: we offer strong tooling for cost controls (batching, caching, quantization recommendations), rollouts, and a consistent dev experience across hosted/dedicated/private. plus, engineered fallbacks for reliability which is key at the edge.
[08:10] Miles Turner: ok pilot inputs — we'll give you prompt corpus for our top 10 use cases, expected qps distribution, and a staging cluster. what else?
[08:19] Priya Khandelwal: that'll get us 80% of the way. we'll need an API key mapping strategy (tenant ids -> redwood keys), list of compliance checks, and success criteria: target latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and a quality threshold on the hallucination metric you care about.
[08:36] Samir Patel: on quality threshold — can you help define automated evals? we prefer an open-source eval harness.
[08:42] Ethan Zhao: yes we have an eval harness and can plug your prompt set in; we'll measure ROUGE/bleu-ish metrics for retrieval tasks and hallucination rates based on a labeled subset.
[08:55] Ava Rodriguez: onboarding timeline recap?
[08:58] Priya Khandelwal: quick recap — priya to send security pack and partner one-pager by monday (2026-09-20); ethan will draft pilot plan and config by 2026-09-24; miles to share staging access and prompt corpus by 2026-09-22; schedule tech deep-dive week of 9/28.
[09:18] Samir Patel: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[09:21] Priya Khandelwal: thanks, we'll follow up with the links and a calendar invite for the deep dive. bye.

End of transcript
